sentences.text:
PROSECUTION STORY:
4.
As per prosecution story, the applicant is stated to have raped the minor daughter of the informant, when she had gone to an orchard alongwith her sister.

On raising of alarm by the sister,
other persons are stated to have reached there.
Seeing them, the applicant is stated to have run away from the scene of occurrence.
The victim is stated to be a person of abnormal mental status.

RIVAL CONTENTIONS:
(Arguments on behalf of applicant)
5. It is argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with a view to cause unnecessary harassment and to victimize him.
It is stated that he has nothing to do with the said offence.
It is stated that FIR is delayed by five months and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
6. It is further argued that the medical report does not corroborate the prosecution story, although it has been taken up after much delay.

Learned counsel has further stated that the instant FIR has been instituted out of animosity, as there is a civil suit bearing Suit No. 819 of 2020 pending between the parties before the Court of Civil Judge (Junior Division) City, Jaunpur.

entities.text: Court of Civil Judge (Junior Division) City, Jaunpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned counsel has next stated that earlier on also, the FIR No. 231 of 2019 was instituted against the applicant by the same informant and the applicant is on bail in the said case.
Learned counsel has further stated that the informant wants to keep the applicant behind the bars out of the said animosity.

Learned counsel has next stated that the victim as per the ossification test report, is stated to be 15 years,
although she is stated to be 13 years of age by the informant.
7. It is further stated that the applicant has no criminal history except the two FIRs instituted by one and the same informant.
It is further argued that there is no evidence, whatsoever, to indicate about the mental status of the victim and she is a normal girl.
Learned counsel has stated that the story as narrated in the FIR cannot be believed.
8. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 8.2.2024.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

(Arguments on behalf of opposite party/State)
9.
Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed the bail application but have not disputed the fact that the said FIRs were instituted by the same informant.

CONCLUSION:

sentences.text: The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

A person's right to life and liberty,
guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because he or she is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.
The said principle has been reiterated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 (10) SCC 51.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, 2022 (10) SCC 51
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned AGA has not shown any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
11. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned AGA for the State.

12. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case that earlier on, the FIR was instituted against the applicant by the same informant and there is civil suit pending between the parties, the evidence on record regarding complicity of the accused, larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

13. Let the applicant- Durgashankar Alias Pandit, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
14. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

15. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

Order Date :- 15.7.2024 Shalini (Justice Krishan Pahal)
